void add_transition(State source, const std::string &symbol_name, State target, Alphabet *alphabet = nullptr)

Add a new transition from source to target labeled by the symbol named symbol_name.

Convenience wrapper mirroring nfa::Nfa::add_transition(), translating symbol_name to a Symbol via the resolved alphabet instead of requiring the caller to translate it themselves.

Unlike the plain-Symbol overloads above, symbol_name is translated separately for each level the transition spans (i.e., levels[source], levels[next_level_after(levels[source])], …, up to but excluding levels[target]), each via the alphabet resolved for that level (see resolve_alphabet): alphabet, when non-null, takes precedence over this->alphabets (used in AlphabetLevels::Mode ::MultiLevel via the level being translated for; ignored in Global mode) over this->alphabet.

If every affected level translates symbol_name to the same Symbol, a single jump transition from source directly to target is added (no new states). Otherwise, since a single jump transition cannot carry a different symbol per level, the jump is unwound into a sequence of ordinary, single-level transitions, each carrying its own level’s translation of symbol_name, through freshly created inner states.

Parameters:

  • source – [in] Source state of the new transition. Must already exist.

  • symbol_name – [in] Name of the symbol labeling the new transition, translated separately for each level the transition spans.

  • target – [in] Target state of the new transition. Must already exist.

  • alphabet – [in] Alphabet to translate symbol_name with on every affected level, taking precedence over this->alphabets/this->alphabet when non-null.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – If no alphabet is available to translate symbol_name for some affected level.

State insert_word_by_levels(State source, const std::vector<Word> &word_parts_on_levels, State target)

Inserts a word, which is created by interleaving parts from word_parts_on_levels, into the NFT from a source state source to a target state target, creating new states along the path of word.

The length of the inserted word equals num_of_levels * the maximum word length in the vector word_parts_on_levels. At least one Word in word_parts_on_levels must be nonempty. The vector word_parts_on_levels must have a size equal to num_of_levels. Words shorter than the maximum word length are interpreted as words followed by a sequence of epsilons to match the maximum length.

Parameters:

  • source – The source state where the word begins. source must already exist and be of a level 0.

  • word_parts_on_levels – The vector of word parts, with each part corresponding to a different level.

  • target – The target state where the word ends. target must already exist and be of a level 0.

Returns:

The state target where the inserted word_parts_on_levels ends.

Words shorter than the maximum word length are interpreted as words followed by a sequence of epsilons to match the maximum length.

Nft &insert_identity(State state, const std::vector<Symbol> &symbols, JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol)

Inserts identity transitions into the NFT.

For each symbol, the result reads the symbol on every level and returns to state, so the inserted loops accept exactly the tuples (w, w, …, w). The representation depends on jump_mode:

  • JumpMode::RepeatSymbol: one jump transition state -symbol-> state spanning all levels, which repeats the symbol on every level. Read the result with JumpMode::RepeatSymbol, not with JumpMode::NoJump or by the fast composition (CompositionMode::FastNoJump), which require jump-free NFTs.

  • JumpMode::NoJump and JumpMode::AppendDontCares: an explicit loop of num_of_levels single-level transitions through fresh inner states. A jump under AppendDontCares would pad the symbol with DONT_CARE, which is no identity.

A one-level NFT gets a single self-loop in every mode. A state on a nonzero level always gets the explicit loop, as a jump must start and end on level 0.

Parameters:

  • state – The state where the identity transition will be inserted. state serves as both the source and target state.

  • symbols – The vector of symbols used for the identity transition. Identity will be created for each symbol in the vector.

  • jump_mode – How to represent the identity, see above.

Returns:

Self with inserted identity.

Nft &insert_identity(State state, const Alphabet *alphabet = nullptr, JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol)

Inserts identity transitions into the NFT, represented according to jump_mode as described at insert_identity(State, const std::vector<Symbol>&, JumpMode).

Parameters:

  • state – The state where the identity transition will be inserted. state serves as both the source and target state.

  • alphabet – The alphabet with symbols used for the identity transition. Identity will be created for each symbol in the alphabet resolved via get_symbols_to_work_with(alphabet, levels[state]) (see resolve_alphabet for the resolution order).

  • jump_mode – How to represent the identity.

Returns:

Self with inserted identity.

  • symbol – The symbol used for the identity transition.

Relation empty <-> True

bool is_deterministic() const

Test whether the transducer is deterministic.

I.e., whether it has exactly one initial state and every state has at most one outgoing transition over every matching symbol. DONT_CARE overlaps every non-epsilon concrete symbol. Overlapping transitions are deterministic only when they lead to the same target state. Checks the whole transducer, not only the reachable part.

inline bool is_complete(const Alphabet *alphabet = nullptr) const

Test for transducer completeness with regard to an alphabet.

A transducer is complete if every reachable state has at least one outgoing transition over every symbol. A DONT_CARE transition covers every non-epsilon symbol.

Parameters:

alphabet – [in] Alphabet to use, resolved via resolve_alphabet(alphabet).

bool is_complete(const utils::OrdVector<Symbol> &symbols) const

A transducer is complete if every reachable state has at least one outgoing transition over every symbol. A DONT_CARE transition covers every non-epsilon symbol.

StateSet post(const StateSet &states, const std::vector<Word> &level_words, const BoolVector &use_level, StateSet *visited_zero_level_states = nullptr, bool epsilon_closure_after = true, JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol, const std::function<bool(State, const std::vector<size_t>&)> &is_early_exit_config = {}) const

Get the set of states reachable from the given set of states over the given vector of level_words (index corresponds to the level).

Levels with the corresponding use_level set to false will be ignored.

This post uses a bitmask use_level to determine which levels to use. Node: Use of use_level si similar to applying a projection of levels whose entries are set to true. It is a general post method that is used by all of its overloads.

Parameters:

  • states – Set of states to compute the post set from.

  • level_words – Vector of words (w_1, w_2, …, w_num_of_levels), one per level, to compute the post set for. The index of the word in the vector corresponds to the level (tape) on which the word is used. The length of the vector must be equal to the number of levels in the NFT.

  • use_level – Bitmask indicating which levels and their corresponding words to use.

  • visited_zero_level_states – Pointer to a set of states that will be filled with the zero-level states that were visited during the post operation. If nullptr, this set will not be filled.

  • epsilon_closure_after – Whether to perform epsilon closure after the post operation.

  • jump_mode – Specifies if the symbol on a jump transition (a transition with a length greater than 1) is interpreted as a sequence repeating the same symbol or as a single instance of the symbol followed by a sequence of DONT_CARE symbols.

  • is_early_exit_config – Optional predicate, called as is_early_exit_config(state, reading_head_positions) for each reached configuration (a state together with the per-level reading-head positions) just before it is expanded. Returning true halts the search immediately and post() returns the states reached so far. This is a general condition: the caller decides what configuration warrants an early exit and captures whatever it needs in the closure. Leave empty for a full post.

Returns:

Set of states reachable from the given set of states over the given words.

inline StateSet post(const StateSet &states, const std::vector<Word> &level_words, StateSet *visited_zero_level_states = nullptr, const bool epsilon_closure_after = true, const JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol, const std::function<bool(State, const std::vector<size_t>&)> &is_early_exit_config = {}) const

inline StateSet post(const State state, const std::vector<Word> &level_words, StateSet *visited_zero_level_states = nullptr, const bool epsilon_closure_after = true, const JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol) const

Get the set of zero-level states reachable from the given zero-level state over the given vector of level_words (index corresponds to the level).

All words on all levels are used and have to be specified.

This post uses all words on all levels.

Parameters:

  • state – Zero-level state to compute the post set from.

  • level_words – Vector of words (w_1, w_2, …, w_num_of_levels), one per level, to compute the post set for. The index of the word in the vector corresponds to the level (tape) on which the word is used. The length of the vector must be equal to the number of levels in the NFT.

  • visited_zero_level_states – Pointer to a set of states that will be filled with the zero-level states that were visited during the post operation. If nullptr, this set will not be filled.

  • epsilon_closure_after – Whether to perform epsilon closure after the post operation.

  • jump_mode – Specifies if the symbol on a jump transition (a transition with a length greater than 1) is interpreted as a sequence repeating the same symbol or as a single instance of the symbol followed by a sequence of DONT_CARE symbols.

Returns:

Set of states reachable from the given set of states over the given words.

StateSet post(const StateSet &states, const std::vector<Word> &level_words, const std::vector<Level> &word_levels, StateSet *visited_zero_level_states = nullptr, bool epsilon_closure_after = true, JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol) const

Get the set of zero-level states reachable from the given set of states over the given vector of level_words.

The levels of the words are specified in word_levels vector. The post is computed only for the words that have a level corresponding to the level of the state. Levels not specified in word_levels are ignored (projected-out)

This post uses a vector word_levels to specify levels of used words. Note: Use of word_levels is similar to applying a projection of levels from the vector word_levels.

Returns:

Set of states reachable from the given set of states over the given words.

bool is_in_lang(const Run &run, bool match_prefix = false, JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol, bool has_epsilon_cycles = true) const

Check whether a run (or its prefix with match_prefix set) is in the language of an automaton.

Warning

If has_epsilon_cycles is unknown, it is recommended leave it set to true. if it is set to false and the automaton does have an epsilon cycle, the query will loop forever.

Parameters:

  • run – The run to check.

  • match_prefix – Whether to also match the prefix of the word.

  • jump_mode – Specifies if the symbol on a jump transition (a transition with a length greater than 1) is interpreted as a sequence repeating the same symbol or as a single instance of the symbol followed by a sequence of DONT_CARE symbols. Dispatches to the dedicated fast algorithm for JumpMode::RepeatSymbol and to the general post()-based algorithm otherwise.

  • has_epsilon_cycles – Whether the automaton has a cycle of epsilon transitions. You can use mata::nft::has_epsilon_cycle() to compute this value if it is not already known. However, be aware that it is linear-time.

Returns:

true if run is in the language of the automaton, false otherwise.

bool is_in_lang_by_levels(const std::vector<Word> &level_words, bool match_prefix = false, JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol, bool has_epsilon_cycles = true) const

Checks whether level_words are in the language of the transducer.

That is, the function checks whether a tuple level_words (word1, word2, word3, …, wordn) is in the regular relation accepted by the transducer with ‘n’ levels (tracks).

JumpMode::RepeatSymbol is handled by an internal dedicated hand-rolled worklist (a constant factor faster on that mode); the other jump modes go through the general post()-based algorithm, which short-circuits on the first accepting configuration.

Warning

If has_epsilon_cycles is unknown, it is recommended leave it set to true. if it is set to false and the automaton does have an epsilon cycle, the query will loop forever.

Parameters:

  • level_words – The words to check.

  • match_prefix – Whether to also match the prefix of the word.

  • jump_mode – Specifies if the symbol on a jump transition (a transition with a length greater than 1) is interpreted as a sequence repeating the same symbol or as a single instance of the symbol followed by a sequence of DONT_CARE symbols.

  • has_epsilon_cycles – Whether the automaton has a cycle of epsilon transitions. You can use mata::nft::has_epsilon_cycle() to compute this value if it is not already known. However, be aware that it is linear-time.

Returns:

true if word is in the language of the automaton, false otherwise.

StateSet read_word(const Run &run, JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol) const

Read a run and return the set of (zero-level) states the transducer ends up in.

The symbols of run.word are interpreted as a single flat word with the tapes interspersed, i.e. symbols cycle through levels 0, 1, …, levels.num_of_levels - 1, 0, 1, … (see mk_level_word_from_word()).

Parameters:

  • run – The run to read.

  • jump_mode – Specifies if the symbol on a jump transition (a transition with a length greater than 1) is interpreted as a sequence repeating the same symbol or as a single instance of the symbol followed by a sequence of DONT_CARE symbols.

Returns:

Set of all reachable zero-level states after reading run to the end on every level. Note: This returns all reachable states, not just final states. Use is_in_lang() if you need to check language membership, or intersect the result with final states manually if needed. Note: The returned set is empty if the run cannot be read to the end.

inline StateSet read_word(const Word &word, const JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol) const

Read a word and return the set of (zero-level) states the transducer ends up in.

The symbols of word are interpreted as a single flat word with the tapes interspersed, i.e. symbols cycle through levels 0, 1, …, levels.num_of_levels - 1, 0, 1, … (see mk_level_word_from_word()).

Parameters:

  • word – The word to read.

  • jump_mode – Specifies if the symbol on a jump transition (a transition with a length greater than 1) is interpreted as a sequence repeating the same symbol or as a single instance of the symbol followed by a sequence of DONT_CARE symbols.

Returns:

Set of all reachable zero-level states after reading word to the end on every level. Note: This returns all reachable states, not just final states. Use is_in_lang() if you need to check language membership, or intersect the result with final states manually if needed. Note: The returned set is empty if the word cannot be read to the end.

StateSet read_word_by_levels(const std::vector<Word> &level_words, JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol) const

Read level_words (one word per level/tape) and return the set of (zero-level) states the transducer ends up in.

Parameters:

  • level_words – The words to read, one per level (tape). Must have the same size as levels.num_of_levels.

  • jump_mode – Specifies if the symbol on a jump transition (a transition with a length greater than 1) is interpreted as a sequence repeating the same symbol or as a single instance of the symbol followed by a sequence of DONT_CARE symbols.

Returns:

Set of all reachable zero-level states after reading every word in level_words to the end on its level. Note: This returns all reachable states, not just final states. Use is_in_lang_by_levels() if you need to check language membership, or intersect the result with final states manually if needed. Note: The returned set is empty if level_words cannot be read to the end.

std::set<Word> get_words(std::optional<size_t> max_length = std::nullopt, JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol) const

Get the set of all words in the language of the automaton whose length is <= max_length.

If you have an automaton with finite language (can be checked using is_acyclic), you can get all words by calling aut.get_words(aut.num_of_states())

The search goes over words, not over paths: runs spelling the same word are kept together however jumps split the word between transitions, so each word is expanded once, and the work is bounded by the number of distinct words of up to max_length transitions spelling them, no matter how many accepting paths each of them has.

Parameters:

  • max_length – Maximum length of words to be returned. Default: “no limit”; will infinitely loop if the language is infinite.

  • jump_mode – Specifies how to interpret the jump transitions.

Returns:

Set of all words in the language of the automaton whose length is <= max_length.

bool make_complete(const Alphabet *alphabet = nullptr, const std::optional<std::vector<State>> &sink_states = std::nullopt)

Make NFT complete in place.

For each state state, add transitions with “missing” symbols from alphabet (symbols that do not occur on transitions from given state) to sink_states[next_level_after(level)] where level == this->levels[state]. If NFT does not contain any states, this function does nothing.

The same symbols are used to complete every level (see resolve_alphabet); there is currently no support for completing different levels to different per-level symbol sets in this overload.

Warning

If alphabet is nullptr and this->alphabets is set in AlphabetLevels::Mode::MultiLevel, resolution throws, since there is no single alphabet to use for every level; pass an explicit alphabet in that case.

Parameters:

  • alphabet – [in] Alphabet to use for computing “missing” symbols, resolved via resolve_alphabet(alphabet).

  • sink_states – [in] The level-indexed vector of sink states, one per level, already existing in the NFT, into which new transitions are added. If std::nullopt, add new sink states.

Returns:

true if a new transition was added to the NFA, false otherwise.

bool make_complete(const utils::OrdVector<Symbol> &symbols, const std::optional<std::vector<State>> &sink_states = std::nullopt)

Make NFT complete in place.

For each state state, add transitions with “missing” symbols from alphabet (symbols that do not occur on transitions from given state) to sink_states[next_level_after(level)] where level == this->levels[state]. If NFT does not contain any states, this function does nothing.

Note

This overloaded version is a more efficient version which does not need to compute the set of symbols to complete to from the alphabet. Prefer this version when you already have the set of symbols precomputed or plan to complete multiple automata over the same set of symbols.

Parameters:

  • symbols – [in] Symbols to compute “missing” symbols from.

  • sink_states – [in] The level-indexed vector of sink states, one per level, already existing in the NFT, into which new transitions are added. If std::nullopt, add new sink states.

Returns:

true if a new transition was added to the NFA, false otherwise.

bool has_no_accepting_path() const

Is no final state reachable from any initial state?

A plain breadth-first search over a visited bit vector that stops at the first final state. This is a pure graph property; whether it coincides with the emptiness of the accepted language (or relation) is a fact about the concrete automaton class, so the leaves expose it under their own names (e.g. mata::nfa::Nfa::is_lang_empty_scc()).

Returns:

true <-> no accepting path exists.

Returns:

true <-> Automaton graph is acyclic.

template<typename Self> bool is_identical (this const Self &self, const Self &other)

Check if this is structuralry identical to other.

Compares only delta, initial and final. This is exact structural equality, including state numbering (so even stronger than isomorphism), essentially only useful for testing purposes.

Note

Templated on Self (deducing this) so that only same-type comparisons compile.

Parameters:

other – [in] The other automaton to compare with.

Returns:

true iff the structural parts of this and other are identical.

template<typename Self> Self & trim (this Self &self, nfa::StateRenaming *state_renaming=nullptr)

Remove unreachable and non-terminating states in-place.

Remaining states are renumbered densely in ascending order.

Note

A state is reachable when the state is the endpoint of a path starting from an initial state. A state is terminating when the state is the starting point of a path ending in a final state.

Note

Every remaining state therefore lies on an accepting path: after trimming, the language is empty iff initial is empty, which is cheaper to test than is_lang_empty().

Note

Reached only through a leaf’s own one-line trim(), on *this, so an lvalue Self suffices here.

Parameters:

state_renaming – [out] Mapping of trimmed states to new states.

Returns:

this after trimming.

template<typename Self> bool is_lang_empty (this const Self &self, nfa::Run *cex=nullptr)

Check whether no accepting path exists, recording a witness in cex when one does.

Parameters:

cex – [out] Counter-example path (and, via the leaf’s get_word_for_path(), word) for a case an accepting path exists.

Returns:

true if no accepting path exists, false otherwise.

Public Static Functions

static inline bool Minimal(const Level lhs, const Level rhs)

Ordering for Levels in NFTs where lower levels precede higher levels.

That is, levels are ordered as follows: 0 < 1 < 2 < … < num_of_levels-1.

static inline bool Next(const Level lhs, const Level rhs)

Ordering for levels in NFTs where lower levels precede higher levels, except for 0 which is the highest level.

That is, levels are ordered as follows: 1 < 2 < … < num_of_levels-1 < 0. This ordering is used when handling intermediate states (with non-zero levels) in NFTs for determining the next lowest level of the next state.

namespace algorithms¶

Concrete NFT implementations of algorithms, such as complement, inclusion, or universality checking.

This is a separation of the implementation from the interface defined in mata::nft. Note, that in mata::nft interface, there are particular dispatch functions calling these function according to parameters provided by a user. E.g. we can call the following function: is_universal(aut, alph, {{'algorithm', 'antichains'}}) to check for universality based on antichain-based algorithm.

In particular, this includes algorithms for:

  1. Complementation,

  2. Inclusion,

  3. Universality checking,

  4. Intersection/concatenation with epsilon transitions, or,

  5. Computing relation.

bool is_included_antichains(const Nft &smaller, const Nft &bigger, const Alphabet *alphabet = nullptr, Run *cex = nullptr, JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol)¶

Inclusion implemented by antichain algorithms.

The operands are read as the flat automata that Nft::unwind_jumps() with the DONT_CARE replacements below would produce, EPSILON being an ordinary letter. When unwinding would change an operand (a jump transition, or a DONT_CARE spelled out over the replacements), the jumps and DONT_CAREs are explored lazily during the search instead: no operand is unwound and DONT_CARE is not expanded over the alphabet. The answer is that of is_included_antichains_unwound().

Parameters:

  • smaller – [in] Automaton which language should be included in the bigger one

  • bigger – [in] Automaton which language should include the smaller one

  • alphabet – [in] Alphabet whose symbols replace DONT_CARE; nullptr for the symbols of both automata without DONT_CARE.

  • cex – [out] A potential counterexample word which breaks inclusion, one symbol per level. When the jumps are explored lazily, the positions of cex->path inside a jump hold Limits::max_state.

  • jump_mode – [out] Specifies if the symbol on a jump transition (a transition with a length greater than 1) is interpreted as a sequence repeating the same symbol or as a single instance of the symbol followed by a sequence of DONT_CARE.

Throws:

std::invalid_argument – when the level vector of an operand does not cover all its states or holds a level that is out of range.

Returns:

True if smaller language is included, i.e., if the final intersection of smaller complement of bigger is empty.

Nft concatenate_eps(const Nft &lhs, const Nft &rhs, const Symbol &epsilon, bool use_epsilon = false, StateRenaming *lhs_state_renaming = nullptr, StateRenaming *rhs_state_renaming = nullptr)¶

Concatenate two NFTs.

Connects lhs and rhs by adding a run of ε-transitions, one per level, from each final state of lhs to each initial state of rhs. The ε is set to epsilon. If use_epsilon is false, remove_epsilon(epsilon) is run on the result, so every transition over epsilon disappears, including the operands’ own transitions labelled with that symbol. Operand transitions over any other symbol are preserved; in particular, with epsilon != EPSILON the operands’ EPSILON transitions survive, which is not the case when epsilon == EPSILON.

Parameters:

  • lhs – [in] First automaton to concatenate.

  • rhs – [in] Second automaton to concatenate.

  • epsilon – [in] Symbol used for the connecting transitions between lhs and rhs.

  • use_epsilon – [in] Whether to keep the connecting epsilon transitions in the result.

  • lhs_state_renaming – [out] Map mapping lhs states to result states.

  • rhs_state_renaming – [out] Map mapping rhs states to result states.

Returns:

Concatenated automaton.

Nft concatenate_eps(Nft &&lhs, const Nft &rhs, const Symbol &epsilon, bool use_epsilon = false, StateRenaming *lhs_state_renaming = nullptr, StateRenaming *rhs_state_renaming = nullptr)¶

Concatenate two NFTs with epsilon transitions, consuming the left operand.

Same result as the copying overload. The left operand’s state posts are moved into the result; the right operand is copied normally. If lhs and rhs are aliased, a controlled snapshot of rhs is taken before lhs is consumed. lhs is left valid but empty after the operation.

Nft concatenate_eps(Nft &&lhs, Nft &&rhs, const Symbol &epsilon, bool use_epsilon = false, StateRenaming *lhs_state_renaming = nullptr, StateRenaming *rhs_state_renaming = nullptr)¶

Concatenate two NFTs with epsilon transitions, consuming both operands.

Same result as the copying overload. The state posts of both operands are moved into the result. If lhs and rhs are aliased, a controlled snapshot of rhs is taken before lhs is consumed, so the result holds both copies. Both lhs and rhs are left valid but empty after the operation.

Nft compose_general(const Nft &lhs, const Nft &rhs, const utils::OrdVector<Level> &lhs_sync_levels, const utils::OrdVector<Level> &rhs_sync_levels, bool project_out_sync_levels = true, JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol, CompositionNormalization normalization = CompositionNormalization::Auto)¶

Composes two NFTs.

This function computes the composition of two NFTs, lhs and rhs, by aligning their synchronization levels. Vectors of synchronization levels must be non-empty and of the same size. The levels of the resulting NFT are formed, iteratively, from the non-synchronizing levels of lhs, followed by the non-synchronizing levels of rhs, followed by the next synchronizing level (if not projected out by setting project_out_sync_levels to true). For example, given lhs with 7 levels, rhs with 8 levels, lhs_sync_levels=<0,2,5>, rhs_sync_levels=<1,4,5>, the resulting NFT levels will correspond to (assuming that we are not projecting out the synchronized levels)

  • rhs level 0

  • synchronized level from level 0 of lhs and level 1 of rhs

  • lhs level 1

  • rhs levels 2 and 3

  • synchronized level from level 2 of lhs and level 4 of rhs

  • lhs levels 3 and 4

  • synchronized level from level 5 of lhs and level 5 of rhs

  • lhs level 6

  • rhs levels 6 and 7

NOTE: If you have only a single synchronization level per NFT, consider compose_fast() for better performance; it reads jump transitions as well.

Operands whose transitions all go to a later level of their round or end it are composed by compose_general_direct() (with more than one aligned level), all others by the pipeline of compose_general_reference(); both accept the same relation.

Parameters:

  • lhs – [in] First transducer to compose.

  • rhs – [in] Second transducer to compose.

  • lhs_sync_levels – [in] Ordered vector of synchronization levels of the lhs.

  • rhs_sync_levels – [in] Ordered vector of synchronization levels of the rhs.

  • project_out_sync_levels – [in] Whether we want to project out the synchronization levels.

  • jump_mode – [in] Specifies if the symbol on a jump transition (a transition with a length greater than 1) is interpreted as a sequence repeating the same symbol or as a single instance of the symbol followed by a sequence of DONT_CARE.

  • normalization – [in] Only CompositionNormalization::Full and Trim change the result: the general composition generates no states of its own for GeneratedOnly to rewrite.

Throws:

std::invalid_argument – When the request is invalid; the same checks as nft::compose() runs, so calling this entry point directly does not skip them.

Returns:

A new NFT after the composition.

Nft compose_general_reference(const Nft &lhs, const Nft &rhs, const utils::OrdVector<Level> &lhs_sync_levels, const utils::OrdVector<Level> &rhs_sync_levels, bool project_out_sync_levels = true, JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol, CompositionNormalization normalization = CompositionNormalization::Auto)¶

The general composition by a pipeline: copies of the operands padded to the common levels by insert_levels(), a whole-round self-loop at each of their zero-level states, their product(), and project_out() of the synchronization levels.

The reference and the fallback of compose_general_direct(); takes the arguments of compose_general().

std::optional<Nft> compose_general_direct(const Nft &lhs, const Nft &rhs, const utils::OrdVector<Level> &lhs_sync_levels, const utils::OrdVector<Level> &rhs_sync_levels, bool project_out_sync_levels = true, JumpMode jump_mode = JumpMode::RepeatSymbol, CompositionNormalization normalization = CompositionNormalization::Auto)¶

The general composition by a direct traversal of the aligned configurations of the two NFTs.

Builds a result with the relation of compose_general_reference(), EPSILON included, without padding copies of the operands: an operand reads its own levels and waits on the others, and a jump transition is read level by level. It covers operands whose transitions all go to a later level of the round or end it, under every jump_mode, with more than one aligned level. DONT_CARE matches every symbol of the other operand, EPSILON included, as in product() (#561); an operand the pipeline inserts no level into may choose its jump again inside it under JumpMode::RepeatSymbol and JumpMode::NoJump, as product() lets it.

Throws:

std::invalid_argument – When the request is invalid, as compose_general().

Returns:

The composition, or std::nullopt for operands outside that domain.

Nft compose_fast(const Nft &lhs, const Nft &rhs, Level lhs_sync_level, Level rhs_sync_level, bool project_out_sync_levels, JumpMode jump_mode, CompositionNormalization normalization = CompositionNormalization::Auto)¶

Composes two NFTs with a single synchronization level, reading their jump transitions in jump_mode.

The levels of the resulting NFT are in the following order:

  • levels of lhs before its synchronization level

  • levels of rhs before its synchronization level

  • the synchronizing level (possibly missing if project_out_sync_levels is true)

  • levels of lhs after its synchronization level

  • levels of rhs after its synchronization level

A jump transition is read lazily, one level at a time: the jumps of a symbol post share a cursor per level they cover after their first one, which reads the symbol of the jump under JumpMode::RepeatSymbol and DONT_CARE under JumpMode::AppendDontCares, and a configuration of the composition pairs such cursors as it pairs states. A level inside a jump thus synchronizes on the symbol the jump reads there. The operands are not copied, and DONT_CARE is not spelled out. Under JumpMode::RepeatSymbol, an EPSILON transition between two zero-level states is a whole round of EPSILON, as under JumpMode::NoJump.

The result has no jump transitions: a jump is unwound into one transition per level, through the result states of the configurations with its cursors, so it reads the same in every jump mode. Its relation is the one of compose_fast_no_jump() on the operands with their jumps unwound in jump_mode (DONT_CARE kept), which is the relation of compose_general() whenever the operands have no EPSILON or DONT_CARE, no jump of jump_mode JumpMode::AppendDontCares reads DONT_CARE on a synchronization level, and, under JumpMode::RepeatSymbol, neither operand with a jump is composed with a one-level operand. The two compositions place EPSILON differently, and compose_general() matches DONT_CARE with EPSILON (#561) and lets an operand composed with a one-level operand choose its jump again inside it.

Parameters:

  • lhs – [in] First transducer to compose.

  • rhs – [in] Second transducer to compose.

  • lhs_sync_level – [in] The synchronization level of the lhs.

  • rhs_sync_level – [in] The synchronization level of the rhs.

  • project_out_sync_levels – [in] Whether we want to project out the synchronization levels.

  • jump_mode – [in] How a jump transition reads the levels after its first one. With JumpMode::NoJump, the operands must not have jump transitions other than fast EPSILON transitions, as in compose_fast_no_jump().

  • normalization – [in] How to normalize the result after the construction; see CompositionNormalization.

Throws:

std::invalid_argument – When a synchronization level is out of range for its operand, when the composition would leave no levels, or, under a jump mode other than JumpMode::NoJump, when a transition goes to an earlier level of its round. The no-jump shape of the operands under JumpMode::NoJump is only checked by MATA_ASSERT.

Returns:

A new NFT after the composition.

struct CompositionSchedule¶
#include <algorithms.hh>

The common level layout of the general composition of two NFTs.

The aligned levels come in blocks, one per synchronization level and one after the last: the levels only lhs reads, then the levels only rhs reads, then the synchronization level, which the last block lacks. The result of the composition has the aligned levels in this order, without the synchronization levels when they are projected out. Example: 

           LHS                         |                    RHS
—————————————–—+——————————————— num_of_levels = 5 | num_of_levels = 4 sync_levels = { 2, 4 } | sync_levels = { 1, 2 } —————————————–—+——————————————— positions: lhs 0, lhs 1, rhs 0, sync (2, 1), lhs 3, sync (4, 2), rhs 3 lhs_new_levels_mask() = { 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1 }, rhs_new_levels_mask() = { 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0 }

Nft construct(const parser::ParsedSection &parsec, Alphabet *alphabet, NameStateMap *state_map = nullptr)¶

Loads an automaton from a single parsed section of the mata format.

Unlike the IntermediateAut overload below, this one reads parsec verbatim: Initial and Final are taken as plain lists of state names and a body line is always a source symbol target triple. State names are therefore arbitrary strings, not subject to the naming markers that IntermediateAut parses; symbol names are still resolved through alphabet, which decides which of them are valid. This overload is also the only one that reads the level metadata: Levels assigns state:level pairs and LevelsNum sets the number of levels, both of which the IntermediateAut path ignores. The two overloads consequently accept different inputs and cannot be merged without changing observable behavior.

Parameters:

state_map – If not nullptr, the map from state names to states, which all overloads and readers fill in the same way. The names it maps beforehand keep their states, each allocated (with the default level) when the input uses its name; a final formula of an IntermediateAut that is true or negates states uses every name of the map it does not negate. Every other name gets the lowest state that the automaton does not have yet and that no name of the map had beforehand, so that it never shares the state of a mapped name, used later or not at all.

std::optional<Nft> parse_explicit_from_mata(std::string_view nft_in_mata, Alphabet *alphabet = nullptr, NameStateMap *state_map = nullptr)¶

Reads an NFT from the .mata format in nft_in_mata with the fast reader of explicit alphabets.

The reader skips mata::parser::parse_mf(), and reads only the inputs whose transitions are source symbol target triples, whose Initial and Final lines list states, and whose Levels and LevelsNum lines give each state at most one level as a decimal number without leading zeros that fits Level. For those, it returns the NFT construct() returns from parse_mf() of nft_in_mata, with the states numbered the same.

Parameters:

  • nft_in_mata – Input with a single @NFT or @NFT-explicit section.

  • alphabet – Alphabet translating the symbol names; nullptr reads them as numbers (IntAlphabet).

  • state_map – If not nullptr, receives the map from state names to states, see construct().

Returns:

The NFT, or std::nullopt when nft_in_mata needs the general reader, as do malformed inputs. state_map is then left unchanged, while alphabet may have learned symbols of the lines read before.

Nft from_nfa_with_levels_zero(const nfa::Nfa &nfa, size_t num_of_levels = DEFAULT_NUM_OF_LEVELS, bool explicit_transitions = true, std::optional<Symbol> next_levels_symbol = {})¶

Create Nft from nfa with specified num_of_levels.

This function takes transition from nfa as transitions between zero level and the first level of NFT. All transition between the remaining levels are created based on the function parameters: explicit_transitions and next_levels_symbol.

Parameters:

  • nfa – NFA to create NFT from.

  • num_of_levels – Number of levels of NFT.

  • explicit_transitions – If true, the transitions between levels are explicit (i.e., no jump transitions, except for the epsilon transitions over all levels).)

  • next_levels_symbol – If specified, it is used as a symbol on transitions after the first level. If not specified, the symbol of the transition is reused.

Returns:

NFT representing nfa with num_of_levels number of levels.

Nft from_nfa_with_levels_advancing(nfa::Nfa nfa, size_t num_of_levels)¶

Creates Nft from nfa with specified num_of_levels automatically.

It assumes that nfa is a representation of an NFT without jump transitions. It assigns to each state the level based on the distance from the initial state. For example, if there are 2 levels, the initial states are level 0, the successor states are level 1, the states after that level 0, etc.

If you only have one level, then it is more efficient to call the constructor that takes Nfa as input.

States unreachable from the initial states get the default level 0: any level is vacuously correct for them.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – if some state should be assigned two different levels or if the final state is not at level 0.

nfa::Nfa create_nfa(const std::string &pattern, const Re2Options &options)

Creates NFA from regular expression using RE2 parser.

At https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax, you can find the syntax of regular expressions with following futher limitations: 1) If you use UTF8 encoding, the created NFA will have the values of bytes instead of full symbols. For example, the character Ā whose Unicode code point is U+0100 and is represented in UTF8 as two bytes c4 80 will have two transitions, one with c4 followed with by 80, to encode it. 2) The created automaton represents the language of the regex and is not expected to be used in regex matching. Therefore, stuff like ^, $, , etc. are ignored in the regex. 3) Only the post-processing steps requested by options are run on the created automaton.

See also

mata::nfa::builder::create_from_regex()

Parameters:

  • pattern – regex as a string

  • options – conversion and post-processing options

struct BodyToken
#include <parser.hh>

One token of a body line, with the flag telling whether the reader read it in quotes.

struct Re2Options
#include <re2parser.hh>

Options of the conversion of a regex to an NFA and of the post-processing of the result.

The defaults reproduce the behaviour of the overloads taking the individual parameters: epsilon transitions removed, the result trimmed and reduced by simulation reduction.

Public Members

bool keep_epsilon = {false}

Translate every instruction of the regex program to a state, with an epsilon transition for each step that consumes no symbol. Otherwise, the regex is converted directly to an NFA without epsilon transitions.

Symbol epsilon = {306}

Symbol representing epsilon transitions.

Encoding encoding = {Encoding::Latin1}

Encoding of the regex. Trim the created NFA. Without epsilon transitions, the conversion only creates states reachable from the initial state, and only a branch that can never match, such as ‘[^\x00-\xff]’ in Latin1, leaves useless states behind.

bool reduce = {true}

Reduce the created NFA by simulation reduction. The reduction costs seconds on regexes with a few thousand states, where the conversion itself takes milliseconds; turn it off for large regexes and when the result is determinized anyway.

class ExplicitSectionReader
#include <explicit-section-reader.hh>

Reads the single section of a .mata input line by line, tokenizing every line as parse_mf() does.

The reader covers only lines that are lists of names, and in the formula mode also the operators and parentheses of transition formulas (&, |, !, (, )), which it splits off as tokens of their own, as parse_mf() does. It gives up on anything else parse_mf() would turn into an operator, on a second section, on a line continuation left open at the end of the input, and on every input parse_mf() rejects. Giving up is reported as Line::Unsupported, so that the caller can hand the input to the general reader, which then either reads it or reports the error.

constexpr size_t hash_mix(size_t value)

Spreads every input bit of value over all of its output bits.

A multiply-xorshift finalizer: the 64-bit variant is the one Boost.ContainerHash uses since 1.81, the 32-bit variant is Murmur3’s fmix32. Without such a finalizer, nearby keys (which is what state identifiers are) stay nearby in the hash space and share hash-table buckets.

template<class Vector>
inline void sort_and_rmdupl(Vector &vec)

Sorts vec and removes its duplicate elements.

std::sort stays the sorting algorithm: it is the fastest of the ones measured on the mixed sizes mata produces, and a specialized sort would have to be restricted to unsigned integral keys anyway, because SymbolPost compares by symbol only and would lose targets under a comparison sort. Already-sorted input is common (ordered construction, conversion from an ordered container), and the linear std::is_sorted check that detects it costs far less than the sort it avoids.

constexpr size_t HASH_SEED{sizeof(size_t) == 8 ? static_cast<size_t>(0xcb'f2'9c'e4'84'22'23'25ULL) : static_cast<size_t>(0x81'1c'9d'c5UL)}

The seed every composite hash of mata starts from.

Composite hashers must not start from the raw hash of their first element: std::hash of an integer is the identity in libstdc++ and libc++, so an unmixed first element would survive into the result and make whole families of keys collide.

struct sorted_unique_t
#include <ord-vector.hh>

Tag selecting the OrdVector constructor that adopts an already sorted, duplicate-free vector.

template<class Key, std::size_t InlineCapacity = std::max<std::size_t>(1, sizeof(std::uintptr_t) / sizeof(Key))>
class SmallOrdVector
#include <small-ord-vector.hh>

A set of keys kept as a sorted, duplicate-free contiguous array, like OrdVector, that stores up to InlineCapacity keys inside the object and allocates only for larger sets.

The object is a pointer-sized buffer plus a 32-bit size word: the buffer holds either the inline keys or a pointer to a heap block, which keeps its capacity in a header in front of the keys. A set lives inline until it outgrows InlineCapacity or a larger capacity is reserved. Like std::vector, it then keeps its heap block when it shrinks, while copies are made in their final form: inline when they fit, otherwise with exact capacity. On 64-bit targets the object ends with four bytes of tail padding, so a [[no_unique_address]] member followed by a 32-bit field packs both into 16 bytes.

Iterators are plain pointers; any operation that grows the set may invalidate them.

template<typename Number>
class SparseSet
#include <sparse-set.hh>

Implementation of a set of non-negative numbers using sparse-set.

This class implements the interface of a set (similar to std::set) using sparse-set date structure, that is, a pair of vectors dense and sparse (… google it). Importantly

  • Insertion and removal are constant time.

  • Iteration is linear in the number of stored elements.

  • It takes a lot of space, the sparse and dense vectors allocate as many indexes as the maximal stored number.

Template Parameters:

Number – Number type: type of numbers contained in the container.

inline bool advance()

Advances all positions to the NEXT minimum and returns true (though the next minimum might be the current state if synchronized_at_current_minimum is false), or returns false if positions cannot be synchronized.

If positions are synchronized to start with, then synchronized_at_current_minimum decides whether to stay or advance further. The general of the algorithm is to synchronize everybody with position[0].

At least one input was pushed since construction or the last reset() (asserted in debug builds); universal synchronization over no inputs is not meaningful. template<typename T, bool TrackInverted = true, size_t MaxMatrixBytes = 200'000'000>
class TwoDimensionalMap
#include <two-dimensional-map.hh>

A two-dimensional map that can be used to store pairs of values and their associated value.

This class can handle both small and large maps efficiently.

Values are stored in a matrix of Cell cells (4 Bytes each, unless T is smaller). The matrix rows are allocated lazily: a row is allocated and zeroed when the first value is inserted into it, so the memory footprint is proportional to the number of first-dimension keys actually used, not to the size of the first dimension. A cell holds the stored value incremented by one; zero means that no value is stored.

The largest matrix we are brave enough to allocate is MaxMatrixBytes Bytes, 200 MB by default, which is 50 million cells of 4 Bytes. For larger dimensions we do not allocate a matrix, but use a single hash table with open addressing and linear probing (hash_storage_), keyed by the pair of keys packed into 64 bits. The table grows geometrically with the number of stored pairs, independently of the dimensions. The product of the dimensions must therefore fit into 64 bits; with keys of at most 32 bits it always does.

Template Parameters:

  • T – Type of the values stored in the map. Must be an unsigned type.

  • TrackInverted – Whether to track inverted indices for the first and second dimensions. To use this feature correctly, the mapping has to be reversible.

  • MaxMatrixBytes – Maximum size of the matrix in Bytes before switching to the hash table.

Public Types

using Cell = std::conditional_t<(sizeof(T) < sizeof(uint32_t)), T, uint32_t>

A matrix cell stores the value incremented by one; zero denotes a missing value.

using Row = std::unique_ptr<Cell[]>

A row is a dynamically sized array: its length is a runtime value, so ‘std::array’ does not apply, and ‘std::vector’ would add a second size and capacity per row.

template<class A>
struct SetHash
#include <utils.hh>

A hasher for std::set, usable as the Hash template argument of unordered containers.

Note

We deliberately do NOT specialize std::hash<std::set<A>> for arbitrary A: the standard only allows program-defined specializations of standard templates when at least one template argument is a program-defined type, so specializing it for e.g. std::set<unsigned> would be undefined behavior (and could silently collide with another library’s specialization for the same type).
